title.en: A medieval imagining of Hannibal’s fleet
title.zh: 中世纪想象中的汉尼拔舰队

alt.en: A manuscript page with two columns of writing and a painted scene of soldiers in boats, a crowned commander, an elephant and a turreted city.
alt.zh: 手稿页有两栏文字；彩绘中有载着士兵的船、戴冠统帅、大象及带塔楼的城市。

caption.en: First Master of the Bible historiale of Jean de Berry and an unknown scribe, The Fleet of Hannibal Sailing to Spain, about 1390–1400, Paris. Tempera, washes, gold leaf and ink; Getty Ms. Ludwig XIII 3, leaf 6.
caption.zh: 让·德·贝里《历史圣经》第一大师与佚名抄写员，《汉尼拔舰队驶往西班牙》，约1390—1400年，巴黎。蛋彩、水洗色、金箔与墨；盖蒂路德维希手稿XIII 3，第6叶。

interpretation.en: A crowned Hannibal, soldiers and battle elephants sail before a fortified city. Made more than sixteen centuries after the Second Punic War, this Parisian manuscript casts the ancient conflict in the visual language of medieval kingship, ships and fortifications.
interpretation.zh: 戴冠的汉尼拔、士兵与战象乘船驶过设防城市。这部巴黎手稿晚于第二次布匿战争逾十六个世纪，用中世纪王权、船只与城防的视觉语言诠释古代冲突。

title.zh: 布匿玻璃与伊特鲁里亚黄金

alt.en: A horseshoe-shaped arrangement of gold beads ends in a white-and-blue glass bearded head beneath a decorated gold cap.
alt.zh: 金珠呈马蹄形排列，下端悬挂蓝白色玻璃胡须人头像，头像上方有装饰金帽。

caption.en: Necklace with a Bearded Head Pendant, Getty 83.AM.1.1. The collection dates the Etruscan gold necklace to 525–500 BCE; Getty’s glass catalogue dates the Punic pendant, probably from Carthage, to the later fourth–third centuries BCE. The present combination was probably assembled in modern times.
caption.zh: 《带胡须人头像坠饰的项链》，盖蒂83.AM.1.1。藏品目录将伊特鲁里亚金项链定为前525—500年；盖蒂玻璃目录将可能产自迦太基的布匿坠饰定为前四世纪后期至前三世纪。现有组合可能为近代重新装配。

interpretation.en: The glass head connects Punic craftsmanship with Mediterranean exchange between Carthage, the Levant and Etruria. Its probable Carthaginian origin and later date distinguish it from the older Etruscan gold beads. Their current arrangement is probably a modern recomposition.
interpretation.zh: 玻璃头像把布匿工艺与迦太基、黎凡特和伊特鲁里亚之间的地中海交流联系起来。坠饰可能产自迦太基，年代晚于伊特鲁里亚金珠；现有装配方式可能形成于近代。
